geneticPoS

Hold your own cis-pQTL MR and colocalization results against the genetic-support criteria of Karim et al., and read the historical launch proportion that goes with them.

Installation 

install.packages("geneticPoS", repos = c("https://daikikumakura.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("DaikiKumakura/geneticPoS")

Quick start

One MR result and one coloc result, joined by the pQTL assay, the outcome GWAS, the genome build and the locus:

library(geneticPoS)

keys <- data.frame(exposure_id = "P1", outcome_id = "D1", build = "GRCh38", locus_id = "L1")
mr <- cbind(keys, mr_id = "M1", target_id = "G1", indication_id = "UC",
            mr_p = 4e-10, l2g_share = 0.67, mesh_similarity = 0.91, measured = TRUE)
coloc <- cbind(keys, coloc_id = "K1", h4 = 0.93)

res <- karim_pos(mr, coloc)
res$candidates[, c("mr_id", "matched_coloc_id", "status", "match_basis", "reference_group", "historical_launch_rate")]
res$benchmark[, c("group", "phase1_n", "launched_n", "relative_success", "rs_lower", "rs_upper")]
  mr_id matched_coloc_id         status       match_basis reference_group historical_launch_rate
1    M1               K1 thresholds_met exact_identifiers       supported              0.5555556

       group phase1_n launched_n relative_success rs_lower rs_upper
1  supported       36         20             5.24     3.88     7.07
2 comparison     7164        760             5.24     3.88     7.07

The candidate meets the criteria, so it is given the launch proportion of the support group of Karim v2 Figure 1a (20/36). This proportion is a past population outcome, not a probability for the candidate.

Overview

geneticPoS is for a statistical geneticist who has their own cis-pQTL MR and colocalization results and wants to know where they stand against the benchmark of Karim et al. v2. The one function, karim_pos(), keeps your rows, matches each MR result to its coloc result, checks the support criteria, and looks up the benchmark. It does not fill in a missing value by guessing: unmatched rows, multiple matches, missing references and unmet thresholds stay in status.

Your results

  1. Prepare a cis-MR result table and a coloc result table. Data frames, CSV and TSV files are accepted. Column names such as pval from TwoSampleMR and PP.H4.abf from coloc are recognized.
  2. Give both tables the pQTL assay, the outcome GWAS, the genome build and a locus identifier. If a locus has several signals, add signal_id to both tables. The MR table also needs the gene symbol and the MeSH ID of the indication.
  3. If the bundled reference lacks something for your locus, pass l2g_share, mesh_similarity and measured (whether the target is measured). Information missing from your tables can be passed in metadata. If you have confirmed from the source papers which MR row belongs to which coloc row, pass that with its evidence in links.

The result

Output Content
candidates Per candidate: verdict, MR p-value, H4, reference value and its source, how the reference was matched, missing items
benchmark Denominators, launches and historical launch proportion of the support and comparison groups of Figure 1a
references The 116 rows of the bundled reference, including the other benchmarks
inputs The input before the reference was resolved

The support group requires MR p ≤ 0.05/47,000,000, H4 ≥ 0.8, L2G share ≥ 0.5, MeSH similarity ≥ 0.8 and a measured target. A single analysis failing a threshold does not by itself put a gene–indication pair in the comparison group. See ?karim_pos for the arguments and the details of the verdict.

Validation and limitations

Details are in reproducibility/INDEPENDENT_PQTL.md.

  • The tests cover row matching, missing values and multiple matches.

  • A public data set (IL23R × Crohn’s disease, one pair) reproduces the verdict: the pair meets the support criteria and returns 20/36 (55.56%). To run it from a clone of the repository:

    Rscript --vanilla reproducibility/check_delange_pqtl.R

  • Limitations. The check on real data covers one pair. How well the package predicts the launch of an individual candidate has not been evaluated. The bundled reference is a processed snapshot; its sources and terms are in DATA_SOURCES.md.

Cite the archived version: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24549534 (all versions). The metadata is in CITATION.cff. The source of the reference benchmark is Karim et al. v2.
